title: Traverse Org Chart Hierarchy with Recursive CTE
description:
Using a recursive CTE, find all employees who report (directly or indirectly) to the CEO (id = 1), along with their level in the hierarchy.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `manager_id`

Output columns: `id`, `name`, `manager_id`, `level`. Order by `level`, `id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, manager_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'CEO',NULL),(2,'VP Engineering',1),(3,'VP Marketing',1),(4,'Lead Dev',2),(5,'Senior Dev',2),(6,'Marketing Mgr',3),(7,'Dev',4);
solution_sql: WITH RECURSIVE reports_to AS (SELECT id, name, manager_id, 1 AS level FROM employees WHERE manager_id = 1 UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, r.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN reports_to r ON e.manager_id = r.id) SELECT id, name, manager_id, level FROM reports_to ORDER BY level, id

test_cases.description: 6 employees report to CEO (directly or indirectly): VP Eng, VP Mktg (level 1); Lead Dev, Senior Dev, Mktg Mgr (level 2); Dev (level 3)

hints: The base case SELECTs direct reports of the target manager; the recursive part joins employees back to the CTE to find their reports.
UNION ALL (not UNION) is required in recursive CTEs; the recursion continues until no new rows are produced.
explanation: The recursive CTE starts with direct reports of the CEO (level 1): VP Engineering and VP Marketing. In the next iteration it finds their reports (level 2): Lead Dev, Senior Dev, Marketing Mgr. In the third iteration it finds level 3: Dev who reports to Lead Dev. No further reports exist so recursion stops. Total 6 descendants.
